newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher not worried by import price rise.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher not worried by import price rise.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher was quoted on Tuesday as saying that the recent rise in German import prices was no cause for concern.

Kuehbacher told "Boerse Online" magazine in an interview that he would not rule out that the Bundesbank may further reduce money market rates if the situation required but added that there was no need for such a move now.
The text of the interview was released ahead of publication in Wednesday's edition of the weekly magazine. The interview was conducted last Wednesday.
Asked if the strong dollar harboured dangers for price stability in Germany, Kuehbacher said: "I don't see that. The most recent rise in import prices is in my opinion not a cause for concern.

"The Bundesbank regards a price rise of up two percent as tolerable, and it does not see this goal in danger. Especially since the situation on the labour market, which we of course also see, speaks against strong inflationary pressure."

Asked if the Bundesbank could give the German economy some stimulus in view of the current stable price outlook, Kuehbacher said: "German money and capital market interest rates are currently lower than they have ever been. I don't want to rule out that we will again reduce money market rates if the situation should require it.
"But at the moment there is no sign of a shortage of demand for credit for investment in expansion. Rather there is strong demand for speculative capital."
